ledger.claim: The driver's own platform record trips the anti-farming guard in POL-NS-07. EV-DPROF-00207 records driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d of 7, which is 4 or more, and 7 against driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 61 works out at 11.5 percent, which is above the 0.08 rate limb. Both limbs of the check are met on this trip's evidence, so this is the second limb of POL-NS-07 engaging, not a borderline call.

Because both limbs of the anti-farming check are met, POL-NS-07 withholds the driver's compensation and routes the case to escalation under POL-NS-09, and it obliges the escalation packet to direct the reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee in full, precisely so that the rider does not fund a dispute the platform has not resolved. EV-FARE-00207 shows the $4.00 sitting at PENDING with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so nothing has been taken from the rider and the packet instruction is that the $4.00 be returned.

Escalation is the correct disposition and is terminal for the automated pipeline: under POL-NS-09 no monetary ruling issues and the disputed cancellation fee is placed on hold rather than collected or refunded, and under POL-GEN-03 ESCALATE is party-relative - the disputed amount is held. On a rider-filed dispute over a fee still at PENDING, that is the outcome the rider presses for, because the $4.00 stays uncollected while the platform's own integrity question on this driver is open.

The escalation trigger is not built on degraded material. EV-DPROF-00207 is COMPLETE with an empty issues list and weight_multiplier 1.0, so there is no POL-GEN-02 discount to apply to the no-show-termination and completed-trip counters, and the escalation rests on a clean artifact rather than on an impairment of the rider's choosing.

The rider's relief here does not run through POL-NS-06, and I do not stretch it to say otherwise: the driver's own telemetry shows a single continuous qualifying in-geofence run of 507 seconds, 06:41:10 to 06:49:37, against the 300 second STANDARD minimum, so there is no waiting-period shortfall. The route to the rider not carrying this charge is the POL-NS-07 anti-farming escalation, not a dwell finding.

Nor does the rider's case run through POL-NS-04, and I do not pretend it does. EV-CHAT-00207 holds four entries and every one is sent by the SYSTEM or the driver; the rider wrote nothing during the waiting window, so limb (a) of the rider-contact clause - a locating or coordinating message from the rider - is not met, and the rider cannot invoke that exoneration on this record.

POL-NS-01 is satisfied on all four limbs, so the cancellation fee is legitimately chargeable and the rider's claim is not supported on the merits. (a) EV-TRIP-00207 records a driver 'arrived' event at 06:41:20. (b) EV-GPS-00207 places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD pick-up geofence from 06:41:10, ten seconds before that event. (c) The continuous in-geofence dwell was 507 seconds, exceeding the 300-second STANDARD minimum. (d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 06:49:37 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, 207 seconds after the required dwell elapsed at 06:46:10.

POL-NS-02's arrival geofence test is comfortably met: the driver's trace holds 52 consecutive qualifying fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, against the three consecutive in-radius fixes the clause requires, and the driver's closest approach to the pin was 14.5 m.

No waiting-period shortfall arises under POL-NS-06: the measured in-geofence dwell is 507 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum, a surplus of 207 seconds, so the full-refund route in that clause is not engaged and no refund follows on this footing.

POL-NS-05 does not catch this driver. The 'arrived' event at 06:41:20 lands on a qualifying in-geofence fix, the dwell having begun only 10 seconds earlier at 06:41:10, so the arrival marker is not false, the waiting clock is correctly started, and the corrected dwell is the full 507 seconds.

POL-NS-03's wrong-entrance route cannot apply, because the clause is confined to a driver stationary OUTSIDE the arrival radius; here the driver was inside the 50 m radius for the whole stop, his nearest fix 14.5 m from the pin, so there is no wrong-face-of-the-building case and the 50%-of-fee goodwill payment is not triggered.

POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider. Its first limb requires a locating or coordinating message FROM the rider in the waiting window, and EV-CHAT-00207 contains none - all four entries are SYSTEM or DRIVER. The driver in any event met the silence directly, messaging 'boss im downstairs at 682' at 06:42:30 and placing an in-app call at 06:45:10 that EV-TRIP-00207 records as unanswered.

Even if limb (a) of POL-NS-04 were met, limb (c) is affirmatively failed on the rider's own track: EV-GPS-00207 places the rider's device a mean 1,900 m from the pin for the whole window with rider_qualifying_fix_count of 0, so the rider was never within the 100 m STANDARD presence radius the clause requires.

The fare line carries no integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d): the $4.00 cancellation fee equals the fee_schedule.resolution_rule figure, being the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00), so there is no basis for down-weighting the fare evidence or for a PARTIAL_REFUND.

EV-ADVIS-00207-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 as the pre-pass records (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), and I disclose that it bears no fact. Its absence does not assist the rider, because the driver's 507-second hold is a single unbroken in-geofence run requiring no accumulation under POL-NS-06(i); a missing advisory merely makes that limb unavailable rather than exonerating anyone.

I must be candid about the driver's remedy rather than assert one the clause forbids. POL-NS-07 would ordinarily pay 80% of the fee - $3.20 of $4.00 - once POL-NS-01 is met and no POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 clause displaces it. But POL-NS-07's anti-farming check is met on this driver's own profile: no_show_terminations_30d is 7 (at or above 4) and 7 divided by completed_trips_30d of 61 is 11.5% (above 8%), so both limbs trip, compensation is WITHHELD and the case routes to escalation under POL-NS-09 with the packet instruction to refund the rider's fee. The fee itself nevertheless remains chargeable on the merits stated above.

replay.note: the advocates' outputs were replayed from an earlier run and not regenerated by this one: only the judge was called, so the figures here measure the judge's behaviour on fixed inputs and not the whole pipeline

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: the $4.00 no-show fee will not be taken from you while this is open, but I cannot simply hand it back either — the case has to go to a human reviewer, and here is why. To the driver: on the merits your fee was properly earned, but your own record is what blocks payment.

On the merits the driver did everything the no-show rule asks. His trip record shows an 'arrived' event at 06:41:20, and the GPS trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD pickup zone from 06:41:10 — so he was at the pin before he tapped. He then held position inside that zone continuously for 507 seconds (8 min 27 s), well beyond the 5-minute STANDARD minimum, and cancelled only at 06:49:37, some three and a half minutes after the waiting clock ran out, recording RIDER_NO_SHOW. He messaged at 06:42:30 and placed an in-app call at 06:45:10 that went unanswered. All four conditions of POL-NS-01 are therefore met, and POL-NS-02, POL-NS-03, POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06 all point the same way: there is no geofence failure, no false arrival marker (the marker falls 10 seconds after geofence entry), no wrong-entrance case (the driver's nearest fix was 14.5 m from the pin), and no waiting-period shortfall (507 s against 300 s, a 207 s surplus). The rider's account that she came down shortly after is not supported by her own device's track, which sits about 1.9 km from the pickup pin across the whole waiting window with zero qualifying fixes inside the 100 m presence radius, and she sent no coordinating message, so POL-NS-04 does not exonerate her. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00207-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 and carries no fact; it does not matter either way, because the driver's hold was a single unbroken run that needed no accumulation under POL-NS-06(i).

What stops the case ending in the driver's favour is POL-NS-07. That clause pays 80% of the fee only if the platform's anti-farming check is clean, and it is not: EV-DPROF-00207 records 7 no-show terminations in the last 30 days against 61 completed trips — 11.5%, over the 0.08 rate limb, with 7 at or above the count limb of 4. Both limbs trip, so compensation is withheld and POL-NS-09 requires escalation.

Under POL-NS-09 the escalation is terminal for the automated pipeline: no money moves, and the disputed $4.00 stays at PENDING — held rather than collected from the rider or refunded to her — while the reviewer examines the driver's pattern. The packet carries POL-NS-07's own instruction that the reviewer refund the rider's cancellation fee in full. Every artifact this ruling rests on is complete at weight 1.0 (trip record, GPS trace, fare breakdown and driver profile), so my confidence is 0.90.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
referrals: POL-NS-07: the anti-farming check is met (7 no-show terminations in 30 days over 61 completed trips, 11.5%), so driver compensation is withheld and the escalation packet must direct the human reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee of SGD 4.00 in full.
